findings.text: The default Claude path for the fast assistant probably breaks. Sessions.js (fast spec, `sdk.env`) no longer spreads `...process.env`. With `mcp_url: ""` and the Claude backend, `door()` returns no env (Agents.js:984, `or_env` is null), so the new merge in Agents.js `options()` hands the SDK an env holding only the two flags: no PATH, no USERPROFILE/HOME, so no Claude login. The proof only ran `openrouter`, where `door()` adds `process.env` back, so it never ran this path. Smallest fix: pass the two flags as top-level `env:` on the spec (that becomes `this.env`, which `door()` already merges last at Agents.js:984/988), and keep `...process.env` out of it.

Doing #1 makes the Agents.js `options()` env re-merge unnecessary, because Sessions.js is the only caller with `sdk.env`. The Sessions.js comment also describes the mechanism wrongly: it says `sdk.env` is `this.env`, but `this.env` is `spec.env` (Agents.js:245).

The fallback can fire on a normal reply. `woken()` tests `USAGE_LIMIT_RE` (`usage limit|rate.?limit|quota|429|exceeded`) against every `done: <the agent's own words>` (Agents.js:661). Right now the owner is talking about usage limits, so a smart reply like "once you hit the usage limit…" moves that session to OpenRouter for good. Match only `error` wakes, or the CLI's exact refusal text.

After the fallback the assistant starts blank and the refused line is lost. `woken()` sets `backing[role] = null` before `wake()`, so `wake()` sees no `old` and spawns "new" with `context: ""` (Sessions.js `wake()`). The 40-line tail is never passed, and the owner's line that Claude refused is never re-sent. The owner hears nothing until they speak again, and then to an agent with no memory of the session. Keep the tail (spawn fresh with `this.tail(s, 40)`) and re-send the last owner line.

Item 2 is not proven as asked. prove.mjs calls `Sessions` directly instead of talking to Dictate on the site headless. The "$ per reply" figures are typed in by hand (prove.mjs:93-96), not measured, which breaks Law 7 (compute, don't recall). The transcript is also off: in prove-results.txt, smart's reply to sentence 3 is word-for-word its reply to sentence 2, and fast answered sentence 2 with "(listening)". The script is probably reading a stale turn's words from `agents.wait`, so we can't tell what the switched agents actually said.

Flipping `SERVEX_SESSION_BACKEND` for a session that already exists still resumes its Claude `backing` session id under the new model (`wake()` resumes whenever the session file exists). Only `woken()` clears it. Clear `backing` whenever `session_model()` differs from the model the agent ran on.

Item 3 asks for a pair (fast, smart), but the readme names one model for both. Local Qwen for the fast assistant (no tools, $0) was never compared. One line saying why luna beats local for fast would close it.

Each of these needs a Servex restart to take effect: the `hire()` fake parent, `parent: "sessions"` on every session agent, and the env-var switch. Nothing in the diff shows where the owner sets `SERVEX_SESSION_BACKEND` from the site, and the owner said the site is the only surface left. A toggle, or at least a line naming where to set it, would help.

On today's default Claude path, the fast assistant loses its two lean flags (`ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`). Sessions.js now puts them in the top-level `env`, but with `mcp_url: ""` and no OpenRouter/local provider, `door()` takes its `!url` branch and sets `env: or_env ? {...} : undefined` (Agents.js:989 in the worktree), so `this.env` is thrown away. The simplest fix is one line in that branch: `env: (or_env || this.env) ? { ...process.env, ...or_env, ...this.env } : undefined`.

The cost numbers in Servex/agents/readme.md (the "default pair" bullet) are wrong: $0.0022 against $0.044 is 20x cheaper, not "5x". prove-results.txt:373 and prove.mjs:495 say "roughly 400x" for the same two figures. These are the numbers the owner would use to pick the after-cutoff pair (Want 3), so they must be right.

Want 2 asked for the proof to run on the site, headless through `Server/browser.mjs`/check_page. prove.mjs instead calls `Sessions.create()`/`say()` directly against a throwaway `Agents` host. The reason it gives (the routes live inside Servex, so testing them needs a restart) is fair, but Want 4 restarts Servex anyway, so one browser run of Dictate after the merge would close this gap.

Want 2 also asked for "real $ per reply", and the proof doesn't deliver that. The key diff read $0.0000 (prove-results.txt:372), and the per-reply figure is a hand-measured range taken from separate calls. This gap is honestly logged as gaps.md #8, but per-reply cost for this model is still unproven live.

Nothing shows the automatic fallback (`woken()`, Sessions.js) working. The code path looks sound: a refused assistant message sets `message.error`, which Agents.js:1289 emits as an `error` event, so it wakes the parent as `error: rate_limit` and matches `USAGE_LIMIT_RE`. But neither prove.mjs nor the task log simulates a refusal. A short test that calls `sessions.woken("error: rate_limit", { from: <fast id> })` would prove the stop → fresh spawn → re-send path.

The proof's second smart reply repeats itself (prove-results.txt:363-365), and the smart agent says it "asked the folder's readme expert" but never answers. The model works for chat, but its tool follow-through is worth a look before the owner relies on it as the only smart assistant.

Agents.js:923 only adds a warning comment about `...this.sdk` replacing `door()`'s `env`; the trap itself stays. Merging `env` in `options()` (`env: { ...door.env, ...this.sdk.env }`) would remove the trap for every future caller, instead of relying on each one reading the comment.

Under the "local" setting the smart assistant stays on Claude, and nothing will move it off when Claude refuses it. `Sessions.js` `session_model()` (diff lines 211-216) only sends the fast role to Qwen and leaves smart on `Usage.pick("smart")`. Meanwhile `woken()` (diff line 171) returns early whenever `session_backend() !== "claude"`, so it never runs its fallback. The header comment (diff lines 82-85) says smart "stays on FALLBACK_MODEL even under local", but the code does not do that. Make `session_model()` return `FALLBACK_MODEL` for smart under "local", or let `woken()` fall back any role that is still on a Claude model.

Requirement 2 asked for a test through Dictate on the site, headless. `prove.mjs` instead calls `Sessions.create()`/`say()` directly against a throwaway `Agents` host, which skips the HTTP routes and the browser half (`ext/Session`). The reason it gives (no Servex restart mid-task) is fair, but nobody has yet watched a reply show up on the site with the switch on. Do that once after the merge and restart.

The "$ per reply" was never measured from these replies. `prove-results.txt` reports a key-level difference of $0.0000 and then quotes a cost that was checked by hand on a separate call. It is honestly labelled, and the gap is logged as `Servex/ext/openrouter/gaps.md` #8, but the per-reply dollar figure the owner asked for is not shown.

`prove-fallback.mjs` calls `woken()` by hand with a made-up `"error: …"` string. In real use the message comes from `Agents.js:1289`. That line emits `String(message.error)`, which for a refused call is the SDK's error code (likely `rate_limit`). That code matches `USAGE_LIMIT_RE`, so the fallback should fire, but the real path was never run. In the real path, `woken()` also stops the agent from inside that agent's own `emit()` (`wake_parent` → `send`), while its result message is still being processed. Check once that this re-entry does not throw or leave a stale "done" behind.

Any 429 or "exceeded" error matches `USAGE_LIMIT_RE`, including a short overload that has nothing to do with the usage cap. That moves the session to OpenRouter for good: `s.fallback` is never cleared, even after the Claude limit resets. This is fine for a cutoff, but it is worth one line in `Servex/agents/readme.md`.

The fallback is decided per session. After a cutoff, every new ✦ session will first get refused by Claude, then respawn. A simpler and more complete version: on the first refusal, `woken()` also writes "openrouter" to `SESSION_BACKEND_PATH`, so every later session starts on OpenRouter straight away.

`wake()` now passes `this.tail(s, 40)` to every fresh spawn, including a brand-new session (diff line 281). That tail can already hold the owner's first line, which is then sent again as the prompt, so the agent sees it twice. The fast assistant also gets a heavier first turn. Pass the tail only when there was an `old` backing id or a `fallback`.

The `Agents.js` `options()` env merge (diff line 37) is a good fix at the root of the problem. Its 11-line comment, and the 12-line comment in `Sessions.js` (diff lines 230-241), describe the same bug twice. One short comment, with a pointer to the other, would do.
Nothing is merged yet: the work is still in the worktree, and `michael/dev` has no `session_backend`. Requirement 4 (merge.mjs, then restart Servex) is still to do once this review passes.

Servex/agents/Sessions.js:181 (`woken()`): the early return `session_backend() !== "claude"` checks the CURRENT setting, not the model the refused agent is actually on. After the first refusal writes `openrouter` to session-backend.txt (line 186), a second session that is still live on Claude and gets refused hits that return and stays silent forever. That is the exact failure this task exists to stop. Check `s.backing_model?.[from.role]` (is it a Claude id?) instead of the global setting.

Requirements item 2 says "talk to Dictate on the site (headless …)". prove.mjs calls `Sessions.create()/say()` in a bare harness with no Servex, no HTTP route and no browser, so the path the owner will actually use is never tested: the ✦ press, `/api/session/*`, and replies turning into chat lines through `watch()→push()`. Once merged and Servex is restarted, run the 3 sentences through the real site with `Server/browser.mjs` or check_page, with session-backend.txt set to `openrouter`.

prove-results.txt:24 does not give a real $ per reply. The key diff read $0, so it falls back to "$0.0000038-$0.0000107 per short reply", measured on a tiny direct `fetch` call. A session-smart reply carries the whole claude_code preset system prompt (thousands of tokens), so its real cost is likely orders of magnitude higher. The same file also says "about $0.0001/call", which contradicts that range. Either read the cost per generation from OpenRouter's activity/generation export after the run, or label the figure as an estimate based on token counts. Don't present it as the real cost.

Sessions.js:186: a single match on USAGE_LIMIT_RE also matches `rate_limit` and `429` from a short Anthropic overload, and it permanently moves every future session off Claude. Nothing undoes that, and the only notice is one chat line in one session. The readme says this is deliberate. Still, the owner should get a visible way to flip back (a line on the board, or a page toggle), not just "the smart assistant can echo into a file".

Sessions.js:122: the regex matches the SDK's assistant `error` string (`rate_limit`, Agents.js:1289), which is good. It does not match `billing_error`, which is what an exhausted Extra-usage or credits plan may report. Consider adding it.

prove-fallback.mjs:466-470 writes and then restores the REAL `%LOCALAPPDATA%/lew42/servex/session-backend.txt`, the same file the live Servex reads. While it runs, any ✦ session the owner opens goes to OpenRouter. A path override (an env var for SESSION_BACKEND_PATH) would keep the test from touching live state.

Simpler-way check: the switch (one text file, then the env var, then "claude") and the fake "sessions" parent that reuses Dispatcher.hire() are about as small as this can be. No second system was built. Good.

Each SDK message still carries its input and output token counts, so a real per-reply dollar figure can be worked out as tokens × OpenRouter's published `/models` price for openai/gpt-6-luna (that is a calculation, not a guess). Print one $ figure per reply.

Ask item 2 says to talk to Dictate "on the site (headless, Server/browser.mjs / check_page; feed text if audio can't be driven)". prove.mjs:1-14 skips the site and calls `sessions.create()`/`say()` directly in a separate process, so the browser → `/api/session/*` → Servex path running on the new switch is never shown. Once the change is merged and Servex restarted (item 4), run the 3 sentences through the real page headless, or say plainly on the card that this step is still owed.

The automatic fallback has only been proven against a hand-written `"error: Claude AI usage limit reached…"` (prove-fallback.mjs:496). In the real code, the text comes from the SDK's `message.error` (Agents.js:1289 → `last_error`), which is an enum string like `rate_limit` or `billing_error`. USAGE_LIMIT_RE does match those. But a non-one-shot agent's failed `result` wakes its parent as `done:` (Agents.js:1211-1214), never `error:`, so a refusal that shows up only as an `is_error` result would be missed. Worth one check against a real refused transcript.

USAGE_LIMIT_RE (Sessions.js diff line 116) also matches the bare word "exceeded" and transient `rate_limit`/429 overloads, and the first match permanently writes `openrouter` to session-backend.txt for every future session, with no automatic way back (readme diff line 335). So an unrelated error such as "context length exceeded" quietly moves all of Dictate off Claude for good. Consider dropping "exceeded", or letting only a clear usage/billing match write the global file.

The cost claims disagree. The Sessions.js comment (diff line 72) says gpt-6-luna is "5x cheaper than Claude Haiku", while the readme (diff line 344) says "20x" ($0.0022 vs $0.044 is 20x). The readme (diff lines 355-357) also says prove.mjs reports a measured $/reply, but prove.mjs prints "unmeasured".

`wake()`'s "model changed → start fresh" check (Sessions.js diff line 280) only works when `backing_model` was recorded. A session saved before this change has no `backing_model`, so flipping the file by hand would still try to resume a Claude session id under gpt-6-luna.

The new readme section (Servex/agents/readme.md, diff lines 308-357) is four dense paragraph-sized bullets. Under "Docs point, they don't explain", the how-it-works detail belongs in a `doc/` page; the readme only needs the setting, the file path, the default pair and a link.

findings.text: Ask item 2 wants "their real $ per reply", but prove-results.txt:21-27 still shows $0.00000000 for every reply because `last_usage` read 0 tokens. `Agents.js:1276` takes usage from each streamed `assistant` message, which on an Anthropic-style stream usually holds the `message_start` counts (input often 0, output 0); the real totals arrive later in `message_delta` and in the turn's `result` event (`usage`, `modelUsage`). Price each reply from the `result` event's usage, or replay one sentence with a raw `fetch` (which gaps.md #8 says does return `usage.cost`) so the card shows at least one measured dollar figure.

Item 4 is not done: `worktree/dictate-without-claude` (c1e352aa) is not merged into michael/dev, and `Servex/agents/Sessions.js` there has no `session_backend`. Until it merges and Servex restarts, the owner's live Dictate still has no switch and no fallback, which is the whole point of the ask.

The proof never goes through the site (prove.mjs:625-636 calls `create()`/`say()` in a separate process). The ask said "talk to Dictate on the site (headless … feed text)". Once merged and restarted, run the same 3 sentences through the real page with `Server/browser.mjs`, or say on the card that this step is still owed.

Simpler and safer trigger: Servex already writes the real weekly and session usage % to `ai/usage.json` (`Servex/Usage.js:40` reads it). Switching to OpenRouter when that reads ~100%, and back when it resets, is computed from real state (law 7). The current trigger, a regex on an `error:` wake (Sessions.js diff line 119), has only been tested with a hand-written string, and dictate-backend.md:388 admits a refusal that arrives as a failed `result` would be missed.

The first match writes `openrouter` to session-backend.txt for good (Sessions.js diff line 189), so after the weekly reset Dictate stays off Claude until someone edits that file by hand, and dictate-backend.md:356 says there is no UI for it. The usage.json check in note 4 would also bring it back on its own.

The code looks right after the earlier rounds: `env` now merges instead of being replaced (Agents.js diff line 31), `local` keeps smart on gpt-6-luna, `woken()` checks the refused role's own model, and a model change starts the agent fresh instead of resuming it. Sessions saved before this change still have no `backing_model` (dictate-backend.md:390); that gap is known and small.

The automatic fallback probably never fires on a real Claude usage-limit refusal. `USAGE_LIMIT_RE` (Sessions.js, diff line 135) only matches an `error:` wake, but a refused turn usually arrives as a `result` with `is_error: true`. For a session agent (not `one_shot`), Agents.js:1211 wakes the parent with `done: <last_text>`, not `error:`, and Agents.js:1570 only stores the reason in `agent.last_error`. Fix: in `woken()`, also test the live agent's `last_error` (`this.servex.agents.live.get(note.from)?.last_error`) against the usage words. The doc's "Open, not fixed here" note (dictate-backend.md, first bullet) names this gap, but it is the main case requirement 1 asks for.

`prove-fallback.mjs` proves nothing about a real refusal. It hand-feeds `woken()` the exact `"error: …"` string the regex was written for (diff lines 575–582), so it can't catch finding 1. Add a case where the wake is `done:` and the agent's `last_error` reads "Claude AI usage limit reached", and make that case pass.

Requirement 2 said to talk to Dictate **on the site** (headless, `Server/browser.mjs` / check_page, typed text is fine). `prove.mjs` calls `Sessions.create()`/`say()` directly in a bare harness instead (diff lines 646–657). Its reason was not wanting to restart the owner's Servex, but requirement 4 restarts Servex anyway. After the merge and restart, run the 3 sentences through the real ✦ panel and save a screenshot plus the replies. Without that, the browser → Servex → session path is untested on OpenRouter.

The first refusal writes `openrouter` into `session-backend.txt` for every future session, for good (Sessions.js `woken()`, diff line 205). The regex also matches `rate.?limit` and `429`, which can be a short, temporary throttle. So one brief 429 could keep Dictate off Claude permanently, and the only way back is deleting a file in `%LOCALAPPDATA%`. Consider matching only the usage-limit wording, or having the file note when Claude resets so sessions can switch back.

`wake()` now skips resuming whenever `backing_model` changes (diff lines 299–300). On the default Claude path, `Usage.pick("smart")` switches between Sonnet and Opus depending on weekly pace (Usage.js:40). Each time it switches, a live smart session restarts fresh with a 40-line tail instead of resuming. A Claude→Claude model change could still resume; only a change between providers needs a fresh start.

The proof's dollar figures are believable: $0.0121 for 6 replies, about $0.002 per reply (prove-results.txt). But the key-level cross-check read $0 in the saved run, while gaps.md #8 and dictate-backend.md say it "landed in the same range ($0.0140 vs $0.0134)". That figure comes from a run that isn't saved. Either save that run or soften the claim.

The Agents.js `options()` env merge (diff line 31) and the `door()` no-URL fix (diff line 46) are correct. Simpler: since session-fast now uses top-level `env`, the `sdk.env` merge line may not be needed. Keep it only if other callers still pass `sdk.env`.

Requirement 3 is done: `openai/gpt-6-luna` for both roles, picked from the eval. But Servex/agents/readme.md only names it inside a long paragraph. One plain line, "After a Claude cutoff, Dictate runs on: fast = gpt-6-luna, smart = gpt-6-luna", would be easier to find quickly.

The automatic fallback probably never fires on a real cutoff. `Agents.js:1570` sets `last_error` from `message.errors` or else `message.subtype`, but a Claude Code usage-limit refusal usually comes back as `is_error: true` with the words in `message.result` ("Claude AI usage limit reached|…") and no `errors`, so `last_error` becomes "success" or "turn failed" and `USAGE_LIMIT_WORDS` never matches (`Sessions.js` `woken()`, diff line 207). Fix: also store `message.result` when `is_error` is set, or check the assistant message's `error` field ("rate_limit" / "billing_error"). Case 3 in `prove-fallback.mjs` sets `last_error` to the refusal text by hand, so it never tests the real result shape.

`last_error` is never cleared after a turn that succeeds (`Agents.js:1204` and `:1570` only ever set it). An agent that once hit a temporary 429, then recovered, still carries that error, so its next ordinary "done:" wake triggers a fallback. Because the fallback also writes `session-backend.txt`, that moves the whole site off Claude for good. Clear `last_error` at the start of each turn, or compare it only against the turn that just ended.

The docs claim a cross-check that the committed results contradict. `doc/dictate-backend.md` (diff line 420) and `gaps.md` #8 both say "$0.0140 vs $0.0134 computed, 6 replies", but `prove-results.txt` reads "key-level diff after 20s: $0.0000, against $0.0121". The comment above the cross-check in `prove.mjs` also still says "when it doesn't, as below, it corroborates". Make the docs match the run that was actually committed.

The flip to OpenRouter is one-way and site-wide. `rate.?limit` and `\b429\b` also match short, temporary throttling, and the only way back is editing a file in `%LOCALAPPDATA%`. The doc admits this. A single-line "Claude is back" switch (a route, or a sentence the smart assistant knows to act on) would make the trade-off safe; it doesn't have to be built here.

Requirement 2 asked to talk to Dictate "on the site (headless … feed text)". `prove.mjs` instead calls `Sessions.create()` and `say()` directly on a throwaway host, and explains why. The spawns, replies and $ are real, but the browser → `/api/session/*` → reply path was never exercised with the switch on. After the Servex restart, a single headless check that types one line into Dictate would close this gap.

The $/reply figures are computed from token counts times the published price, not billed. Fast turn 2 shows 795 input / 268 output tokens for a single short sentence, which suggests the per-agent diff of the running `modelUsage` total sometimes counts tokens against the wrong turn. The total ($0.012 for 6 replies) is still believable, and gpt-6-luna is clearly cheap enough for the pick to stand.

The case numbering in `prove-fallback.mjs` disagrees with itself: the header comment calls case 2 "THE REAL CASE" and case 3 the rare `error:` crash, while the code and `prove-fallback-results.txt` run them the other way round.

Requirement 4 (worktree → check_page → merge → restart Servex) can't be checked from the diff alone. The proof paths point at `worktrees/dictate-without-claude`, which suggests a worktree was used. Confirm that the merge and restart actually happened before landing.

Simpler option: the `Agents.js` env-merge fix (diff lines 26–31) is now one of two places that join `door.env` and `sdk.env`; Sessions already moved to top-level `env`. With no caller left passing `sdk.env`, that extra merge line could go, so there is one path. The rest (the switch in `session_model()`, the file-then-env setting, the readme's pair) is a reasonable size and does what item 1 and item 3 asked.

Item 2 asked to talk to Dictate on the site, headless. prove.mjs calls `Sessions.create()`/`say()` directly on a bare `Agents` host, and its own comment at prove-fallback.mjs:~93 admits that this harness never runs Servex's `watch()` → `push()` wiring. That wiring is what turns a gpt-6-luna reply into a chat line the owner sees in Dictate, so the one path the owner said they will depend on is unproven. Once item 4's restart is done, run the 3 sentences once through the real `POST /api/session/new` and `/api/session/say` with the backend set to openrouter (Server/browser.mjs or plain fetch, using a fresh session), shoot the Dictate panel showing the replies, then reset the file.

The core works. With the backend set to openrouter, Servex/agents/Sessions.js `session_model()` puts both roles on `openai/gpt-6-luna`. prove-results.txt shows 6 real, sensible replies at about $0.002 each, and Sessions.test.mjs still passes (13 checks). The model names `Usage.pick()` returns ("claude-sonnet-5", "claude-opus-5-5") start with "claude", so the `startsWith("claude")` guard in `woken()` holds for both roles.

The automatic fallback is one-way and site-wide. One refusal anywhere writes `openrouter` to session-backend.txt (Sessions.js `woken()`), and nothing ever writes it back after Claude's weekly reset. If nobody notices, every later session stays on gpt-6-luna. A simpler safety: write the reset time next to the word (or an expiry), and have `session_backend()` ignore the file once that time has passed.

The `local` mode (fast assistant on `local/qwen2.5-coder`) is never exercised. Neither proof spawns it, and nothing checks that the local model server is running. If it isn't, the fast assistant goes quiet. Either prove it once or say plainly in doc/dictate-backend.md that it is untested.

Servex/agents/doc/dictate-backend.md has gone stale against the code. The "Automatic fallback" section says the match is "an `error:`-kind wake only", but `woken()` now also checks `last_error`.
